findings.title: Crash: list mixing a multi-row and a 1-row dataset with default line fmt dies in scipy pchip; smoothing is order-dependent (guard checks only first dataset)
findings.description: plot.py's static line-interpolation guard (scalar-fmt branch, ~line 2326) is `if xform[0].shape[0] > 1:` -- it checks ONLY the FIRST dataset before calling interp_array_list on ALL datasets. Consequences, all verified: (a) hyp.plot([25-row, 1-row]) with the default '-' fmt crashes with an uncaught scipy ValueError from hypertools/_shared/helpers.py:140 interp_array -> pchip -- cryptic, no hint of which dataset or the fmt='.' workaround; (b) the reverse order [1-row, 25-row] silently SKIPS interpolation for every dataset (per-artist point counts [1, 25] vs [900] when the same 25-row data is plotted alone), so line smoothing depends on list order; (c) the fmt-LIST branch directly below checks per-dataset (`xi.shape[0] > 1`) -- the scalar branch should do the same. Discovered while regression-testing closed issue #192 (whose verbatim all-1-row repro IS fixed: 16 artists render). Realistic trigger: plotting subject trajectories alongside a single-observation dataset (group mean, single text embedding).

findings.title: Residual of closed #259: `import hypertools` still mutates matplotlib rcParams (backend_fallback True -> False)
findings.description: Issue #259 ('importing hypertools updates matplotlib rcParams') was closed COMPLETED, and style params are indeed untouched, but importing hypertools still flips rcParams['backend_fallback'] from True to False -- a side effect of hypertools/plot/backend.py calling matplotlib.use() at import time (mpl.use() sets backend_fallback=False). Verified with a baseline taken AFTER `import matplotlib.pyplot`, so the mutation is attributable to hypertools, not pyplot. Impact: after importing hypertools, a later invalid backend assignment raises instead of falling back -- a small but real change to global matplotlib behavior from a bare import.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import copy, matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
before = copy.deepcopy(dict(matplotlib.rcParams))
import hypertools
after = dict(matplotlib.rcParams)
print({k: (before[k], after[k]) for k in before if repr(before[k]) != repr(after[k])})"

findings.title: hyp.load() on an unsupported binary file (e.g. .png) raises a raw _pickle.UnpicklingError from dill internals instead of a clear 'unsupported file type' error
findings.description: Images are intentionally out of scope for hyp.load() (issue #273 was closed with maintainer-narrowed scope: sklearn+seaborn named datasets only), but the failure mode for an image path is a leaked internal: _load_local's pickle sniff (suffix list + first byte b'\\x80') correctly rejects the PNG, then sources.load_local_file's extension/sniff fallback ends up unpickling the bytes via dill and surfaces `_pickle.UnpicklingError: A load persistent id instruction was encountered, but no persistent_load function was specified.` -- no mention of the file, the unsupported extension, or what formats ARE supported (docstring: pickle/.geo, .npy/.npz, .csv/.tsv/.txt, .json, .parquet, .mat, .xlsx/.xls). Should raise HypertoolsIOError naming the extension and the supported list.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
arr = np.zeros((8, 8, 3)); arr[::2, ::2] = [1, 0, 0]
plt.imsave('/tmp/tiny_x8.png', arr)
hyp.load('/tmp/tiny_x8.png')"
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError: unsupported file type '.png' -- hyp.load() reads .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls and pickled .geo/.pkl (or similar)
findings.actual:
File ".../dill/_dill.py", line 453, in load
    obj = StockUnpickler.load(self)
_pickle.UnpicklingError: A load persistent id instruction was encountered, but no persistent_load function was specified.

findings.title: Hosted *_model example datasets are sklearn-1.0.2-era pickles: loading under the 1.0 stack (sklearn 1.8.0) emits InconsistentVersionWarning ('might lead to breaking code or invalid results')
findings.description: hyp.load('wiki_model') (and by construction nips_model/sotus_model, same vintage) unpickles LatentDirichletAllocation/CountVectorizer/Pipeline estimators created under scikit-learn 1.0.2 into the installed scikit-learn 1.8.0, emitting sklearn's InconsistentVersionWarning for each estimator. sklearn explicitly does not support cross-version unpickling ('Use at your own risk'). The load succeeds and returns a Pipeline, but a scientist following docs/examples that use *_model datasets gets a wall of scary warnings and no guarantee of valid topic-model outputs. Recommend re-fitting/re-pickling the hosted *_model files under the 1.0 dependency floor (or documenting the warning as expected + verified-harmless).
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; m = hyp.load('wiki_model'); print(type(m).__name__)"
findings.expected: Model loads with no version-compatibility warnings (pickle created under the supported sklearn range), or documentation stating the warning is expected and outputs verified
findings.actual: sklearn/base.py:463: InconsistentVersionWarning: Trying to unpickle estimator LatentDirichletAllocation from version 1.0.2 when using version 1.8.0. This might lead to breaking code or invalid results. ... (repeated for CountVectorizer, Pipeline) then: Pipeline

findings.title: Model-spec kwarg naming is inconsistent across sibling dispatchers: hyp.align/hyp.manip use model=, hyp.cluster/hyp.reduce/hyp.normalize use the function's own name; first arg is x vs data
findings.description: Signatures on this branch: cluster(x, cluster='KMeans', ...), reduce(x, reduce='IncrementalPCA', ...), normalize(x, normalize='across', ...) vs manip(data, model='ZScore', ...), align(data, model='HyperAlign', ...). A user who learns hyp.align(data, model={'model': 'Procrustes'}) and tries the same with cluster gets `TypeError: cluster() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model'` with no pointer to the correct kwarg (cluster=). Positional use works everywhere, and the dict-spec grammar consistently uses 'model' as its key, which makes the top-level kwarg divergence more surprising. For a 1.0 API freeze this is worth either aliasing (accept model= everywhere, warn on conflict) or documenting the convention prominently.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
x = np.random.randn(30, 4)
hyp.cluster(x, model={'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 2}})"
findings.expected: Either accepted (model= alias) or an error suggesting the cluster= kwarg
findings.actual: TypeError: cluster() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model'

findings.title: hyp.plot figures are pyplot-unmanaged yet every figure carries fig.number == 1
findings.description: After creating 3 figures in a loop (closed #264's scenario -- the actual bug IS fixed: distinct objects, distinct content), plt.get_fignums() == [] (figures deliberately not registered with pyplot -- avoids the old leak) but each figure still exposes fig.number == 1, and plt.figure(1) creates an unrelated new figure. Harmless for savefig workflows, but fig.number is matplotlib's documented handle for pyplot lookup, so a stale duplicated value invites confusion (e.g. plt.close(fig.number) semantics). Either strip the attribute or register real numbers.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
figs = [hyp.plot(np.random.randn(20, 3), '.', show=False) for _ in range(3)]
print(plt.get_fignums(), [f.number for f in figs], [f is plt.figure(1) for f in figs])"
findings.expected: Consistent state: either managed figures with unique numbers, or no misleading .number attribute

findings.title: Unknown hyp.plot kwargs surface as matplotlib internals ('Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument ...') rather than a hypertools-level message
findings.description: Deliberate misuse hyp.plot(x, animate=True, soundtrack='epic.mp3') (a plausible guess given open issue #163) raises AttributeError from matplotlib's Line2D.set. The message does name the offending kwarg (so it is actionable), but it leaks the backend artist class, does not mention hyp.plot, and surfaces from inside the draw path. Contrast with the excellent hypertools-authored animate-style error ('unknown animate style ...; valid styles are ...'). A cheap pre-validation pass or a try/except re-raise naming hyp.plot would align the two experiences.
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.plot(np.random.randn(30, 4), animate=True, soundtrack='epic.mp3', show=False, duration=1, frame_rate=5)"
findings.expected: Error mentioning hyp.plot received an unexpected keyword argument 'soundtrack' (and, ideally, that audio is not a supported feature)
findings.actual: AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'soundtrack'

findings.title: Remaining open-issue functionality absent from 1.0 -- all explicitly maintainer-deferred 2026-07-07; none blocks release
findings.description: Desired functionality still missing on this branch, per real checks: #111 keypress labeling of live streams (no key_press_event anywhere -- grep verified), #112 nearest-labeled-point decoding for streams (no decode code in streaming.py; hyp.predict is unrelated forecasting -- run verified), #163 animation soundtrack (no audio code; the ffmpeg-mux prerequisite verified present: mp4 export works via ffmpeg 8.1.2), #225 first-class bootstrap/HOP kwarg (workaround verified: animate='morph' over resamples works in 3-D AND 2-D), #113 the composite brain-decoding vision (2 of 4 sub-pieces shipped: streaming + LSL ingestion, both verified end-to-end here). Block-1.0 judgment: NO for all five -- each carries an explicit maintainer deferral comment ('defer', 'punt for a future release', 'do not implement for now') dated 2026-07-07, effort labels are set (low/medium/high), #111/#112 are 'low priority', and #225/#163 have working workarounds or no renewed demand. 'All desired functionality present' holds for 1.0 in the sense that every remaining ask is a deliberately deferred enhancement, not a gap the release claims to cover.
findings.repro:
gh issue list --repo ContextLab/hypertools --state open --limit 100  # 5 issues: 225,163,113,112,111
grep -rn key_press_event /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/  # empty
grep -rni 'soundtrack|audio' /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/plot/ /Users/jmanning/hypertools/pyproject.toml  # empty
grep -n decode /Users/jmanning/hypertools/hypertools/io/streaming.py  # empty
findings.expected: n/a (enhancement classification for the release decision)
findings.actual: 5 open issues, all enhancements with maintainer deferral comments; verification commands above all return empty (features absent) while the shipped sub-pieces (streaming, LSL, morph) all pass real runs
